quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When stopping behind a vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move forward.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Stop quickly right behind the vehicle.
Stay about four car lengths behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you. The vehicle could back up suddenly, or you may need space to move away from another vehicle coming from behind.

questions.question: If you ride a three-wheeled motorcycle or have a sidecar, why should you not ride too far to the right of your lane?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side of a motorcycle. Riding too far right can cause the sidecar to run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: When packing items on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items toward the front of your load. Loads should be over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, how should a group of motorcyclists ride?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a single-file formation.
In a side-by-side formation.
Using both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Switch to a single-file formation when taking curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is used on straightaways.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Speed up.
Reduce speed.
Lean your shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down. Close the throttle and use both brakes if needed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show traffic rules. They have white backgrounds with black letters or symbols. Examples include speed limit signs. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of your lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see better and to be more visible. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Brake hard on the front brake to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes to slow down on slippery surfaces. Squeeze the front brake lever gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly than normal.
Start slowing earlier than normal.
Increase your following distance.
Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, the motorcycle is heavier and responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down earlier, and increase following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: At high speeds.
After riding for a long time.
Far from home.
On short trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: How can you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to stop car drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: The center portion of a traffic lane often has:

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars.
The safest spot for motorcycle riders.
Where most accidents happen.
The area where drivers least see motorcyclists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane often has debris and oil drippings from cars. Other hazards like manhole covers can also be found in the center of the lane.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your following distance.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a position that lets oncoming traffic see you. Stay back from other vehicles so you can react quickly. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: Which reason for using your horn is not a good idea?

options.text: A driver in the next lane is too close to the car ahead.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your path. Use it if a driver next to you is too close to the car ahead, if someone sits in a parked car, or if a pedestrian is in the street. Don't use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to turn.
Don't drag your feet on the road.
Avoid looking at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean with your turn. Keep your feet off the road to stay in control. Always watch for other traffic on the road.

questions.question: Which lane position should always be avoided?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No lane position should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No lane position should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best, and no position should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: In normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, stay at least four seconds behind the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same lane position throughout the curve.
Always stay in the left portion of the lane.
Always stay in the right portion of the lane.
Know that the best path may not follow the road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know that the best path may not follow the road curve.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions can change at any time. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve does not always follow the road's curve.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you prepare for turns.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Help you avoid wind from other vehicles.
Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, you should stay how far behind the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: If it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Speed up.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Move to the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane can be slippery when wet because of oil. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: The group takes up less space on the road.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to be separated.
A tight group gets to the destination faster than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tight group gets to the destination faster than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than a spread-out group because it uses less road space, is easier to see, and riders stay together at traffic lights and during passes.
